record.statement: Determine whether stationary wake-chain configurations have linear window variance below criticality and a power saving at and above criticality.
record.statement_caveat: As with the free chain, a fixed global particle count requires a restriction on observation windows for a positive uniform lower bound. The stationary and transient free ensembles are distinct source questions.
record.status_search: Focused searches on 2026-09-07 for ARW density, cutoff, local limits, hyperuniformity and incompressibility; four later primary papers read at stated theorem scope. No certificate of present openness.
record.title: Hyperuniformity transition in stationary ARW wake states

record.independent_check: Under the uniform k-subset comparison law, E I_x=k/N and E I_x I_y=k*(k-1)/(N*(N-1)); substitution yields the displayed variance. This comparison law is not asserted to be the ARW stationary distribution.
record.method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation
record.obstruction: The literal all-window lower bound is false; the meaningful small-window transition is unresolved. Exact global covariance cancellation alone cannot prove a subvolume variance bound.
record.result: Every wake-chain state has the same total k. On a cycle, the complement-of-one-site window therefore has variance rho_N*(1-rho_N)<=1/4 under the unique stationary law, where rho_N=k/N; the whole torus has variance zero. More generally, translation invariance forces sum_y Cov(I_x,I_y)=Cov(I_x,k)=0, but this finite-volume cancellation does not imply mesoscopic hyperuniformity. For comparison, uniform k-subsets have Var(S_B)=|B|*rho_N*(1-rho_N)*(N-|B|)/(N-1), which is volume order for |B|=o(N).
